```{r}
# 1. Grab all CSV file paths
csv_files <- fs::dir_ls(speed_folder, glob = "*.csv")

# 2. Process each file with data.table speed
speed_binned_list <- csv_files %>% 
  map(function(file_path) {
    
    # Extract the file name statically
    file_name <- fs::path_ext_remove(fs::path_file(file_path))
    
    # Open dataset and collect directly into a data.table
    dt <- as.data.table(open_dataset(file_path, format = "csv") %>% collect())
    
    # Calculate the 10ms bins and aggregate down instantly
    # data.table handles this entirely in optimized C memory
    binned_dt <- dt[, .(
      speed = mean(speed),
      direction = round(mean(direction))
    ), by = .(time_ms = floor(time_ms / 10) * 10)]
    
    # Add the source file name identifier
    binned_dt[, source := file_name]
    
    return(binned_dt)
  })

# 3. Efficiently bind all datasets together and sort
speed_binned <- rbindlist(speed_binned_list)
setorder(speed_binned, source, time_ms)

# (Optional) Convert back to a standard tibble/dataframe if you prefer working with dplyr later
speed_binned <- as_tibble(speed_binned)





speed_binned <- speed_binned %>% mutate(time_ms = time_ms/1000)
pre <- -20
post <- 20

library(data.table)

# 1. Convert to data.table
setDT(speed_binned)
setDT(sound_starts)

# 2. Define the explicit windows inside sound_starts
sound_starts[, `:=`(
  window_start = continuous_start + pre,
  window_end   = continuous_start + post
)]

# 3. Perform a non-equi join
# This looks for matches where speed_raw$sample falls between window_start and window_end
df_segments <- sound_starts[
  speed_binned, 
  on = .(source, window_start <= time_ms, window_end >= time_ms),
  nomatch = NULL, # Acts like an inner_join
  allow.cartesian = TRUE
]

# 4. Post-join cleanup and relative time calculation
# Note: data.table renames the join columns to the target names, so window_start is actually your original 'sample'
df_segments[, `:=`(
  time_relative = window_start - continuous_start,
  stim_id = trial_type
)]

# Clean up the artificial window columns if you don't need them
df_segments[, c("window_start", "window_end") := NULL]

# Convert to tibble and clean
df <- as_tibble(df_segments) %>%
  filter(Animal %in% Animal_list) %>%
  mutate(
    rel_time = round(time_relative, 2),
    speed_raw = speed,
    speed = abs(speed)
  ) %>%
  select(-time_relative)

# Per-trial baseline Z-score:
# baseline is every timepoint before -1 s,
# calculated independently for each source and trial.
df <- add_baseline_zscore(
  data = df,
  value_column = "speed",
  group_columns = c("source"),
  time_column = "rel_time",
  baseline_end = -1,
  zscore_column = "sz"
)

# Add shock-direction, fear, and optogenetic labels
res2_speed <- df %>% mutate(speed_direction = direction) %>% 
  select(-any_of("direction")) %>%
  left_join(shock, by = "Animal") %>%
  mutate(
    fear = if_else(
      direction == str_remove(stim_id, "^Opto_"),
      "cs+",
      "cs-"
    ),
    Opto = if_else(
      str_starts(stim_id, "Opto"),
      "opto",
      "no"
    ),
    time_bin = rel_time
  ) %>% filter(stim_id %in% c("Downsweep","Upsweep")) %>% filter_out(source %in% exclusion_list)
 
 res2_speed_raw <- df %>%
  select(-any_of("direction")) %>%
  left_join(shock, by = "Animal") %>%
  mutate(
    fear = if_else(
      direction == str_remove(stim_id, "^Opto_"),
      "cs+",
      "cs-"
    ),
    Opto = if_else(
      str_starts(stim_id, "Opto"),
      "opto",
      "no"
    ),
    time_bin = rel_time
  ) 
 

speed_binned %>% distinct(source)


speed_binned %>%
  filter(source == "8181_naive") %>%
  summarise(min_time = min(time_ms), max_time = max(time_ms))

sound_starts %>%
  filter(source == "8181_naive") %>%
  select(source, continuous_start, trial_number) %>% arrange(continuous_start)
```

```{r}
df <- df %>% mutate(time_relative = rel_time) 

shock <- read_csv(r"(I:\Data\aligned\extra\Shock_direction.csv)") %>% select(Animal = Animal2, direction) %>% mutate(direction = paste0(direction,"sweep"))   %>% mutate(Animal = as.character(Animal))


# 1. Calculate baselines safely
baselines <- df %>% 
  group_by(source) %>% 
  filter(between(time_relative,-5,-0.1)) %>% mutate(speed = abs(speed)) %>% 
  summarise(
    base_mean = mean(speed, na.rm = TRUE), 
    base_sd = sd(speed, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop" # Cleanly ungroups for future joins
  ) %>% 
  # If sd is exactly 0 (complete freezing), turn it into NA to prevent Inf values
  mutate(base_sd = ifelse(base_sd == 0, NA_real_, base_sd))

# 2. Join and calculate Z-scores explicitly
res2_speed <- df %>% 
  select(!direction) %>% 
  left_join(shock, by = "Animal") %>% # Explicit join key assumed here
  mutate(
    fear = ifelse(direction == stringr::str_remove(stim_id, "^Opto_"), 'cs+', 'cs-'),
    Opto = ifelse(str_starts(stim_id, 'Opto'), 'opto', 'no'),
    time_bin = time_relative
  ) %>%   mutate(speed = abs(speed)) %>% 
  # Explicitly map the baseline values to the matching source & trial
  left_join(baselines) %>%
  mutate(pz = (speed - base_mean) / base_sd)
```

```{r}
    end_time   = last(rel_time),
    duration   = end_time - start_time,
    nomov_prop = mean(speedcat == "nomov"),
    .groups = "drop"

  # actual immobility periods > 1 s
  filter(duration >= 1,
         nomov_prop >= 0.75)

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(slider)

param_grid <- crossing(
  duration_thresh = seq(0.1, 1, length.out = 9),
  nomov_thresh = seq(0.70, 1, by = 0.05)
)

# Prepare data
dat <- res2_speed %>%
  filter(
    condition == "recall",
    between(rel_time, -5, 5)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    nomov = speed < 0.5
  ) %>%
  group_by(source, trial_number) %>%
  arrange(rel_time, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    dt = median(diff(rel_time))
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

grid_results <- map_dfr(
  seq_len(nrow(param_grid)),
  function(i) {
    
    duration <- param_grid$duration_thresh[i]
    prob <- param_grid$nomov_thresh[i]
    
    n_samples <- round(duration / unique(dat$dt))
    
    events <- dat %>%
      group_by(source, trial_number) %>%
      arrange(rel_time, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
      mutate(
        nomov_prop = slide_dbl(
          nomov,
          ~ mean(.x),
          .after = n_samples - 1,
          .complete = TRUE
        ),
        qualifying = nomov & nomov_prop >= prob,
        new_event = qualifying &
          !lag(qualifying, default = FALSE)
      ) %>%
      filter(new_event) %>%
      ungroup() %>%
      mutate(
        period = ifelse(rel_time < 0, "pre", "post")
      ) %>%
      count(period, name = "n") %>%
      complete(
        period = c("pre", "post"),
        fill = list(n = 0)
      )
    
    tibble(
      duration_thresh = duration,
      nomov_thresh = prob,
      pre = events$n[events$period == "pre"],
      post = events$n[events$period == "post"]
    )
  }
) %>%
  mutate(
    difference = post - pre,
    ratio = post / pmax(pre, 1)
  )

ggplot(grid_results,
       aes(duration_thresh, nomov_thresh, fill = ratio)) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(ratio,2)), size = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = unique(grid_results$duration_thresh)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = unique(grid_results$nomov_thresh)) +
  labs(
    x = "Minimum duration (s)",
    y = "Minimum no-movement proportion",
    fill = "Post / pre"
  ) +
  theme_classic()
```

```{r}

# ============================================================
# Pre-stimulus movement-state analysis for res2_speed
#
# Goal:
#   Test whether the post-stimulus speed response differs
#   depending on whether the animal was:
#     - consistently running forward before the stimulus
#     - consistently running backward before the stimulus
#     - still / mixed-direction before the stimulus
#
# This script:
#   1. Defines several pre-stimulus classification windows.
#   2. Requires stable direction within the chosen window.
#   3. Classifies each trial as forward/backward/still.
#   4. Computes delta speed relative to that trial's own pre-stimulus speed.
#   5. Produces raw-speed and delta-speed plots.
#
# Important:
#   - rel_time == 0 is the stimulus alignment time.
#   - `source` is included in the trial ID because trial_number
#     may repeat across sessions.
#   - The shaded grey area in each plot is the window used to
#     classify the animal's pre-stimulus movement state.
# ============================================================

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(forcats)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# SETTINGS
# ------------------------------------------------------------

condition_to_use <- "recall"

# Time shown in the plots:
plot_window <- c(-1.5, 2.0)

# Baseline used only to establish a source-specific noise level.
# This is intentionally separate from the pre-stimulus state window.
baseline_window <- c(-5, -1)

# Several classification windows to compare.
# A gap before time 0 reduces the chance that movement beginning
# exactly at sound onset determines the pre-stimulus category.
classification_windows <- tibble(
  window_name = c(
    "Early pre-stimulus: -1.0 to -0.5 s",
    "Middle pre-stimulus: -0.8 to -0.3 s",
    "Late pre-stimulus: -0.4 to -0.1 s"
  ),
  window_start = c(-1.0, -0.8, -0.4),
  window_end   = c(-0.5, -0.3, -0.1)
)

# Minimum absolute signed speed needed to consider an animal moving.
# This threshold is in the units of speed_raw, which appear to be deg/s.
# Change after inspecting the speed distribution if necessary.
speed_threshold <- 1

# A trial is called forward/backward only when this fraction of samples
# in the classification window has the same direction.
# Example: 0.75 means at least 75% of samples need to be > +threshold
# or < -threshold, respectively.
stable_direction_fraction <- 0.75

# Post-stimulus interval summarized in the final per-trial response plot.
response_window <- c(0.1, 0.6)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# PREPARE DATA
# ------------------------------------------------------------

speed_data <- res2_speed %>%
  filter(
    condition == condition_to_use,
    between(rel_time, min(baseline_window[1], plot_window[1]),
            max(plot_window[2], response_window[2]))
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    trial_id = interaction(source, Animal, trial_number, drop = TRUE),
    rel_time = as.numeric(rel_time)
  )

# Check whether all expected columns are available.
required_columns <- c(
  "source", "Animal", "trial_number", "condition",
  "rel_time", "speed_raw"
)

missing_columns <- setdiff(required_columns, names(speed_data))

if (length(missing_columns) > 0) {
  stop(
    "res2_speed is missing required column(s): ",
    paste(missing_columns, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# SOURCE-SPECIFIC BASELINES
#
# These are useful for inspecting pre-stimulus movement relative
# to each source's normal signed-speed level.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

source_baselines <- speed_data %>%
  filter(between(rel_time, baseline_window[1], baseline_window[2])) %>%
  summarise(
    baseline_speed = mean(speed_raw, na.rm = TRUE),
    baseline_sd = sd(speed_raw, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_baseline_samples = sum(!is.na(speed_raw)),
    .by = c(source, Animal)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    baseline_sd = if_else(
      is.na(baseline_sd) | baseline_sd == 0,
      1,
      baseline_sd
    )
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# FUNCTION: CLASSIFY PRE-STIMULUS STATE
#
# The category is based on:
#   1. Mean signed speed in the chosen pre-stimulus window.
#   2. Fraction of samples with consistent positive/negative speed.
#
# forward:
#   mean pre-speed > +threshold AND >= stable_direction_fraction
#   of samples are > +threshold.
#
# backward:
#   mean pre-speed < -threshold AND >= stable_direction_fraction
#   of samples are < -threshold.
#
# still/mixed:
#   all other trials, including low-speed and inconsistent-direction trials.
# ------------------------------------------------------------
classify_trials <- function(data, source_baselines,
                            window_start, window_end, window_name,
                            speed_threshold, stable_direction_fraction) {

  pre_window_data <- data %>%
    filter(between(rel_time, window_start, window_end)) %>%
    select(-any_of(c("baseline_speed", "baseline_sd", "n_baseline_samples"))) %>%
    left_join(
      source_baselines %>%
        select(source, Animal, baseline_speed),
      by = c("source", "Animal")
    )

  pre_window_data %>%
    summarise(
      pre_speed = mean(speed_raw, na.rm = TRUE),

      forward_fraction = mean(
        speed_raw > speed_threshold,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

      backward_fraction = mean(
        speed_raw < -speed_threshold,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

      stationary_fraction = mean(
        abs(speed_raw) <= speed_threshold,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

      n_samples_pre_window = sum(!is.na(speed_raw)),

      baseline_speed = first(baseline_speed),

      .by = c(source, Animal, trial_number, trial_id)
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      pre_speed_minus_baseline = pre_speed - baseline_speed,

      movement_state = case_when(
        pre_speed_minus_baseline > speed_threshold &
          forward_fraction >= stable_direction_fraction ~ "forward",

        pre_speed_minus_baseline < -speed_threshold &
          backward_fraction >= stable_direction_fraction ~ "backward",

        TRUE ~ "still / mixed"
      ),

      movement_state = factor(
        movement_state,
        levels = c("backward", "still / mixed", "forward")
      ),

      classification_window = window_name,
      classification_start = window_start,
      classification_end = window_end
    )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# CLASSIFY TRIALS FOR EVERY WINDOW
# ------------------------------------------------------------

trial_states_all <- classification_windows %>%
  mutate(
    trial_state = purrr::pmap(
      list(
        window_start,
        window_end,
        window_name
      ),
      ~ classify_trials(
        data = speed_data,
        source_baselines = source_baselines,
        window_start = ..1,
        window_end = ..2,
        window_name = ..3,
        speed_threshold = speed_threshold,
        stable_direction_fraction = stable_direction_fraction
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  select(trial_state) %>%
  unnest(trial_state)

# Print how many trials fall in each category for each window.
print(
  trial_states_all %>%
    count(classification_window, movement_state) %>%
    group_by(classification_window) %>%
    mutate(
      fraction_of_trials = n / sum(n)
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# BUILD PLOTTING DATA
#
# delta_speed is calculated relative to each trial's own mean
# speed in the classification window:
#
#   delta_speed = speed_raw - pre_speed
#
# Therefore:
#   - each trial is centered relative to its own pre-stimulus state
#   - post-stimulus changes are easier to compare
#   - raw traces will differ before zero by design
#   - delta traces should be interpreted as within-trial changes
# ------------------------------------------------------------

speed_with_states <- speed_data %>%
  filter(between(rel_time, plot_window[1], plot_window[2])) %>%
  inner_join(
    trial_states_all %>%
      select(
        source, Animal, trial_number, trial_id,
        classification_window,
        classification_start,
        classification_end,
        movement_state,
        pre_speed,
        pre_speed_minus_baseline,
        forward_fraction,
        backward_fraction,
        stationary_fraction
      ),
    by = c("source", "Animal", "trial_number", "trial_id")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    delta_speed = speed_raw - pre_speed
  )

# Mean and SEM at each time point.
plot_summary <- speed_with_states %>%
  summarise(
    mean_raw_speed = mean(speed_raw, na.rm = TRUE),
    sem_raw_speed = sd(speed_raw, na.rm = TRUE) /
      sqrt(sum(!is.na(speed_raw))),

    mean_delta_speed = mean(delta_speed, na.rm = TRUE),
    sem_delta_speed = sd(delta_speed, na.rm = TRUE) /
      sqrt(sum(!is.na(delta_speed))),

    n_trials = n_distinct(trial_id),
    .by = c(
      classification_window,
      classification_start,
      classification_end,
      rel_time,
      movement_state
    )
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# PLOT 1:
# RAW SIGNED SPEED BY PRE-STIMULUS MOVEMENT STATE
#
# Interpretation:
#   Groups differ before time zero partly by construction:
#   they were defined using pre-stimulus signed speed.
#
# This plot is useful to inspect the actual running trajectories.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

raw_speed_plot <- ggplot(
  plot_summary,
  aes(
    x = rel_time,
    y = mean_raw_speed,
    colour = movement_state,
    fill = movement_state
  )
) +
  geom_rect(
    aes(
      xmin = classification_start,
      xmax = classification_end,
      ymin = -Inf,
      ymax = Inf
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    fill = "grey70",
    alpha = 0.22
  ) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    colour = "grey55",
    linewidth = 0.4
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(
      ymin = mean_raw_speed - sem_raw_speed,
      ymax = mean_raw_speed + sem_raw_speed
    ),
    alpha = 0.17,
    colour = NA
  ) +
  geom_line(
    linewidth = 0.85
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ classification_window,
    ncol = 1
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(
      "backward" = "#377EB8",
      "still / mixed" = "#666666",
      "forward" = "#E41A1C"
    )
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "backward" = "#377EB8",
      "still / mixed" = "#666666",
      "forward" = "#E41A1C"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Raw signed running speed by pre-stimulus movement state",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Grey shading = classification window. ",
      "Forward/backward requires mean speed beyond ±",
      speed_threshold,
      " and at least ",
      stable_direction_fraction * 100,
      "% of samples in the same direction."
    ),
    x = "Time from stimulus onset (s)",
    y = "Mean signed running speed (deg/s)",
    colour = "Pre-stimulus state",
    fill = "Pre-stimulus state",
    caption = paste0(
      "Dashed vertical line: stimulus onset (0 s). ",
      "Shaded bands: ±SEM across time-point observations."
    )
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

print(raw_speed_plot)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# PLOT 2:
# DELTA SPEED RELATIVE TO EACH TRIAL'S PRE-STIMULUS SPEED
#
# Interpretation:
#   delta_speed = current signed speed - that trial's mean speed
#   in the shaded pre-stimulus classification window.
#
# A positive value means movement became more forward than before.
# A negative value means movement became more backward/slower than before.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

delta_speed_plot <- ggplot(
  plot_summary,
  aes(
    x = rel_time,
    y = mean_delta_speed,
    colour = movement_state,
    fill = movement_state
  )
) +
  geom_rect(
    aes(
      xmin = classification_start,
      xmax = classification_end,
      ymin = -Inf,
      ymax = Inf
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    fill = "grey70",
    alpha = 0.22
  ) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    colour = "grey55",
    linewidth = 0.4
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(
      ymin = mean_delta_speed - sem_delta_speed,
      ymax = mean_delta_speed + sem_delta_speed
    ),
    alpha = 0.17,
    colour = NA
  ) +
  geom_line(
    linewidth = 0.85
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ classification_window,
    ncol = 1
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(
      "backward" = "#377EB8",
      "still / mixed" = "#666666",
      "forward" = "#E41A1C"
    )
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "backward" = "#377EB8",
      "still / mixed" = "#666666",
      "forward" = "#E41A1C"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Stimulus-evoked change in signed running speed",
    subtitle = "Each trial is centered on its own mean speed in the grey pre-stimulus classification window.",
    x = "Time from stimulus onset (s)",
    y = "Change from pre-stimulus speed (deg/s)",
    colour = "Pre-stimulus state",
    fill = "Pre-stimulus state",
    caption = paste0(
      "Positive values: more forward movement than pre-stimulus level. ",
      "Negative values: more backward movement or less forward movement."
    )
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

print(delta_speed_plot)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# PLOT 3:
# PROPORTION OF TRIALS IN EACH CATEGORY
#
# This helps determine whether a classification window generates
# enough trials in forward and backward categories for comparison.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

category_counts <- trial_states_all %>%
  count(classification_window, movement_state) %>%
  group_by(classification_window) %>%
  mutate(
    proportion = n / sum(n)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

state_counts_plot <- ggplot(
  category_counts,
  aes(
    x = classification_window,
    y = proportion,
    fill = movement_state
  )
) +
  geom_col(
    colour = "white",
    linewidth = 0.35
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = paste0(n, " trials")),
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
    colour = "white",
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "backward" = "#377EB8",
      "still / mixed" = "#666666",
      "forward" = "#E41A1C"
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::percent_format()
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Trial classification counts across pre-stimulus windows",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Stable direction criterion: at least ",
      stable_direction_fraction * 100,
      "% of samples beyond ±",
      speed_threshold,
      " deg/s."
    ),
    x = "Pre-stimulus classification window",
    y = "Proportion of recall trials",
    fill = "Pre-stimulus state"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

print(state_counts_plot)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# TRIAL-LEVEL POST-STIMULUS RESPONSE
#
# One value per trial:
#
#   response_delta =
#       mean signed speed from 0.1 to 0.6 s
#       minus
#       mean signed speed in the pre-stimulus classification window
#
# This is preferable to treating every 10-ms sample as independent.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

trial_post_responses <- speed_with_states %>%
  filter(between(rel_time, response_window[1], response_window[2])) %>%
  summarise(
    post_speed = mean(speed_raw, na.rm = TRUE),
    pre_speed = first(pre_speed),
    response_delta = mean(delta_speed, na.rm = TRUE),
    .by = c(
      source,
      Animal,
      trial_number,
      trial_id,
      classification_window,
      movement_state
    )
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# PLOT 4:
# PER-TRIAL POST-STIMULUS DELTA SPEED
#
# Each dot is one trial. Large points show animal-level means.
# This prevents a single animal/session with many trials from
# visually dominating the result.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

animal_response_summary <- trial_post_responses %>%
  summarise(
    animal_mean_response = mean(response_delta, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_trials = n(),
    .by = c(
      Animal,
      classification_window,
      movement_state
    )
  )

post_response_plot <- ggplot(
  trial_post_responses,
  aes(
    x = movement_state,
    y = response_delta,
    colour = movement_state
  )
) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    colour = "grey50",
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_jitter(
    width = 0.12,
    alpha = 0.18,
    size = 1.5
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = animal_response_summary,
    aes(
      x = movement_state,
      y = animal_mean_response,
      fill = movement_state
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    shape = 21,
    colour = "black",
    stroke = 0.5,
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ classification_window,
    ncol = 1
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(
      "backward" = "#377EB8",
      "still / mixed" = "#666666",
      "forward" = "#E41A1C"
    )
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "backward" = "#377EB8",
      "still / mixed" = "#666666",
      "forward" = "#E41A1C"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Trial-level post-stimulus speed change by pre-stimulus state",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Response window: ",
      response_window[1],
      " to ",
      response_window[2],
      " s after stimulus. Small dots = trials; large dots = animal means."
    ),
    x = "Pre-stimulus movement state",
    y = "Post-stimulus speed change from pre-stimulus level (deg/s)",
    colour = "Pre-stimulus state",
    fill = "Pre-stimulus state"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

print(post_response_plot)

# OPTIONAL: SAVE ALL OUTPUTS
# ------------------------------------------------------------


```
